title: The 5-Day Fascism Experiment
description: Could you be manipulated into joining a totalitarian regime? In 1967, a high school teacher conducted a terrifying experiment that proved how easily human nature can succumb to absolute control. 🤯 Are we really as immune to brainwashing as we think?
script:
We comfort ourselves with the soothing delusion that we would have resisted the rise of historical atrocities, believing our modern education and morality make us immune to the psychological traps of totalitarianism. But this is an uncomfortable truth: you are far more susceptible to brainwashing than you think.

In April 1967, at Cubberley High School in Palo Alto, California, history teacher Ron Jones faced an unsettling question from his sophomore class: how could ordinary German citizens claim ignorance of the Holocaust? To answer, Jones did not assign a textbook; instead, he initiated a covert, real-world sociological simulation called 'The Third Wave.'

What followed was a terrifying descent into fascism that took only five days. On Monday, Jones introduced strict classroom discipline, training students to sit at attention and answer questions in three words or fewer. On Tuesday, he established a collective identity, introducing a rigid, wave-like salute and the mantra: 'Strength through discipline, strength through community.' Surprisingly, the students did not resist; they embraced the order.

By Wednesday, the experiment spiraled entirely out of Jones's control. The movement grew from 30 students to over 200, drawing in teenagers from other classes. Students voluntarily created membership cards and established an internal secret police. They began actively policing each other’s behavior, reporting 'traitors' who failed to salute or who questioned the movement’s authority. Dissidents were put on mock trials, and the school hallway turned into a space of intimidation.

On Thursday, recognizing that he had accidentally fostered a highly aggressive, functioning totalitarian regime that was actively turning on its own classmates, Jones knew he had to stop. He told the students that 'The Third Wave' was a nationwide movement and invited them to a Friday rally to watch their presidential candidate speak on television.

On Friday, hundreds of students packed into the auditorium. Instead of a candidate, Jones turned on a blank television screen. After a tense silence, he revealed the truth: they had been manipulated into acting exactly like the citizens of Nazi Germany. He then projected historical footage of Nuremberg rallies. The room fell into stunned, weeping silence as the students realized how easily they had surrendered their democracy, individuality, and morality in less than a week.
